prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Everything verifies clean. The task is complete — here is the final report.

## Report: MCP-built blog site in Umbraco.Bench

**What was built** — entirely through the Umbraco MCP server for schema and content, with code only for the Razor rendering layer (per the required order: model → content → restart → views):

- **Schema (all via MCP):** 6 document-type folders per AGENTS.md (Pages/Blocks/Compositions/Data/Repositories/Repository Items); data types for text, textarea, rich text, date, image picker, and two `DropDown.Flexible` types (spacing, background); a `bodyBlocks` BlockGrid data type; 4 block element types (`heroBlock`, `textBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`) plus a `blockSettings` settings element (anchor/spacing/background) wired via `settingsElementTypeKey`; document types `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost` with templates assigned.
- **Content (all via MCP, all Published):** media folder "Blog" with 7 Unsplash images from `unsplash/` (photographer credits in captions); front page "Blog" at `/` (hero + intro text blocks, then a "Latest posts" card grid); two posts — **"Why MCP Is Awesome"** at `/why-mcp-is-awesome/` and **"Why MCP Is Awesome for Editors"** at `/why-mcp-is-awesome-for-editors/` — each with 5 block-grid blocks (text, image, quote, text, image) using spacing/background settings and an anchor id.
- **Rendering (Umbraco's own pipeline):** `@await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body")` → stock blockgrid chrome → per-block adapter partials in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/` mapping to plain models in `Models/Blocks/` → ViewComponents (`Hero`/`Text`/`Image`/`Quote`) rendering `Views/Shared/Components/*/Default.cshtml`. No custom renderers, no wrapper models. Tailwind v4 built via `npm run build` into `wwwroot/dist/`.

**How to view it:**
- Site: https://localhost:44317/ (front page + post cards), https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome/, https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome-for-editors/ — all return 200
- Backoffice: https://localhost:44317/umbraco — admin@example.com / 1234567890
- The site is currently running (`dotnet run --project /c/code/benchmark/Umbraco.Bench/Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco --launch-profile "Umbraco.Web.UI"`)

**Verified working:** all three pages return 200; every block renders through the block-grid pipeline with settings applied (spacing/background classes, anchor ids); signed crop URLs (`GetCropUrl`) for all images; zero "Could not render component" fallbacks anywhere.

**Anything not working:** Nothing outstanding. One issue was found and fixed along the way: the Quote component view file went missing from disk after an initially successful write, which caused a `quoteBlock` render fallback on both posts; the file was restored, the project rebuilt, Umbraco restarted, and both quotes now render correctly. The only build warnings are pre-existing ImageSharp package vulnerability notices (NU1902/NU1903), unrelated to this work.
